stem: Which ONE of the following is the most commonly used non-invasive test to diagnose acute deep vein thrombosis?
expl: Venous duplex (B-mode compression + Doppler) is the standard non-invasive test for acute DVT — non-compressible vein with absent flow.

why.B: A handheld Doppler gives flow sounds only, no images.
why.C: Isotope scanning is not used for DVT.
why.D: Plethysmography is obsolete for DVT diagnosis.

stem: A 35 pregnant multipara woman complains of longstanding pain, swelling for 5 years. What is the best examination position for varicose veins?
expl: Varicose veins fill with gravity, so they are examined with the patient STANDING (inspection and palpation).

why.D: Trendelenburg's position (head down) empties the veins — used in the tourniquet test, not for inspection.

stem: 51-year-old man who underwent abdomino-perineal resection for low rectal cancer 5 days ago, was complaining of chest pain and dyspnea. Physical examination was normal. CBC and cardiac enzymes were normal. Temp: 37.2, BP:85/50 mmHg, pulse: 120 beat/min. Which of the following is the most common appropriate diagnostic investigation?
srcNote: (Surgical Complications) increased risk of PE post OP
expl: Post-op (pelvic cancer surgery) chest pain, dyspnea, hypotension and tachycardia with normal enzymes → PE → CT pulmonary angiography (spiral CT chest).

why.B: Shows RV strain but doesn't confirm PE.

stem: A 45-years-old man who was diagnosed to have pelvic tumor with right lower limb deep venous thrombosis two years ago, presents with signs and symptoms of chronic venous insufficiency (pain, limb swelling and varicose veins) Which one of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
expl: CVI after a previous DVT (here with a pelvic tumour) = secondary (post-thrombotic) CVI — the deep system is abnormal.

why.A: There is no arterial disease in the history.
why.D: The history points to a single secondary cause.

stem: Scenario of venous case that you duplex scan for him. What is the expected reflux?

opts.t: >1s for deep vein and >0.5 s for superficial and perforating
<1s for deep vein and <0.5 s for superficial and perforating
<1s for superficial and perforating and <0.5 s for deep vein
>0.5s for deep vein and >1 s for superficial and perforating

expl: Pathological reflux on duplex = > 1 s (1,000 ms) in the deep veins (common femoral, femoral, popliteal) and > 0.5 s (500 ms) in the superficial and perforating veins.

stem: An obese man has had a history of varicose veins on thighs for two years now. He has refused treatment for varicose veins. What is the possible complication if left untreated?
srcNote: ( Venous diseases) Choice D is blank in the source.
expl: Keyed superficial thrombophlebitis — a common complication of untreated varicose veins (along with progression to CVI, skin changes, ulceration and bleeding).

why.B: Ulceration occurs with advanced CVI, usually at the medial malleolus (gaiter area) — possible, but the key chose thrombophlebitis.

stem: A 37-year-old woman presents with progressive left leg swelling for 2 years. On examination, the left leg is larger than the right, she has a buffalo hump, and you cannot pinch the skin over the toes, the swelling is non-pitting. You worked her up and diagnosed her with primary lymphedema. Which of the following is the best treatment modality?
srcNote: (Venous diseases) Source note (Final 437 F Q45 (p. 89)): The abbreviated recall calls the condition "primary lymphadenopathy" and gives: A. Extensive massage with elastic compression A
expl: Lymphedema is treated conservatively first: complete decongestive therapy — manual lymphatic drainage, multilayer low-stretch wrapping, exercise and skin care — then maintenance compression garments.

why.A: Diuretics don't remove protein-rich lymph and are not effective.
why.B: Lymphovenous shunting is a selective later option.
why.C: Excisional surgery is reserved for refractory cases.

stem: 40-year-old female with varicose veins asked you when would her condition improve. What is the most appropriate thing to say?
expl: Varicose veins are progressive; the only remission described is after pregnancy and delivery.

why.A: Stockings relieve symptoms but don't make the veins regress.
why.D: Weight loss helps symptoms, not regression.

stem: A 35 years old female house wife and mother of 2 children noticed bluish swelling in both limbs during her second pregnancy. They were associated with pain from prolonged standing. Her mother and grandmother also had varicose veins. Physical examination revealed bilateral varicose veins. Which of the following is the risk factor for this case?
srcNote: ( venous disease) Other source key (Final 434 A Q28 (p. 163)): A. Pregnancy. D. Family history of varicose vein. Both A and D are correct. A could be the more relevant since she noticed it in her pregnancy.
expl: Keyed family history: her mother and grandmother had varicose veins — heredity is a strong risk factor (~90% risk when both parents are affected). Pregnancy and multiparity also contribute.

why.A: Pregnancy contributes, but the key chose family history.
why.C: Not a risk factor in itself.
why.D: Also a risk factor, but the key chose family history.

stem: A 67-years-old female who had a pelvic tumor resected last year presents with bulging veins in the left lower limb. You ordered a duplex scan which showed a significant reflux in the saphenous vein. What is the best next step in management?

opts.t: Endovenous ablation of left great saphenous vein

expl: Varicose veins after pelvic tumour surgery raise suspicion of SECONDARY disease from iliac vein obstruction/compression → image the pelvic veins with CT venography before treating the superficial reflux.

why.A: Abdominal US doesn't assess the iliac veins well.
why.C: Ablating the GSV could remove a collateral pathway if the iliac vein is blocked.

stem: Scenario about varicose veins where the reflux at the saphenofemoral junction. What is the level of stocking?
srcNote: ( Venous disease) Abbreviated source recall; only two answer choices are supplied.
expl: Reflux starting at the saphenofemoral junction needs compression covering the thigh → thigh-high stockings.

why.B: Panty-hose length is used for pelvic/iliac involvement or pregnancy.

stem: A 24 y/o male patient was admitted the surgery trauma unit with multiple injuries 4 weeks ago. He developed sudden onset of chest pain and shortness of breath. His BP: 85/50 mmHg, pulse 110/min, oxygen saturation is 85% on air room, and there is evidence of DVT in the left lower limb. After fluid bolus was given his BP increased to 90/60 mmHg. A CT lung was done and showed a massive pulmonary embolism. Which one of the following is the treatment of choice?
expl: Source key: LMWH — PE with BP responding to fluids is treated with anticoagulation. (Truly massive PE with persistent shock would need thrombolysis.)
